components.name: Web client
responsibilities: React and TypeScript single-page app in frontend/, built with Vite and served by nginx in deployment
Sign-in, registration of the first account and user administration

Keeps the session alive: calls POST /auth/refresh once 80% of the access token's lifetime (from sign-in or the last refresh to its expires_at) has passed, 12 minutes for the 15-minute default, and on a 401 from an API request refreshes once and retries that request a single time

Runs at most one refresh at a time across all its open tabs: tabs coordinate through the browser's Web Locks API and share the refresh's result through a BroadcastChannel, so other tabs and concurrent 401 retries wait for and reuse it
When a refresh is rejected, shows the sign-in form with a short 'session expired' notice and returns the user to the page they were on after signing in again
Start form of a requirements interview asks only for the repository, the branch and what needs to be done; it no longer loads an intake or asks for the kind of task and per-kind answers

Flows page: lists top-level task flows (by their current name) and chats, and a task flow's requirements or onboarding interview, requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery children with pending, skipped and linked-from-another-task marks (a requirements task flow lists only its requirements child until it is finalized); opens chats, sessions and onboardings in a panel; the Requirements and Onboarding filters list task flows of that origin through the origin filter, and old-shape requirements and onboarding flows from before this change are shown only in the All view

Requirements session panel shows the kind of task currently recorded, or 'not set yet' while none is, updated as the interviewer records or changes it, and shows the 409 detail when finalizing without a kind

Shows the requirements review flow with its rounds and, when the user continued anyway, the contradictions that remained; shows the review's status, contradiction questions and any reviewer error in the requirements and onboarding sessions, with a retry button for a failed review round
Asks for confirmation in a warning modal window before finalizing with force while the review reports contradictions or has failed

Shows an open task flow as running and highlights it, and each of its children, as waiting for the user and with the unresolved findings marker as GET /workflows reports them, instead of deriving them from the children's sessions; opens the waiting child's questions from the highlight
Old-shape requirements and onboarding flows from before this change and their stages are only listed and opened, with no waiting-for-user highlight and no unresolved findings marker
Opens the next stage from a session's returned IDs: the architecture session, the API design session, or the delivery of a bugfix or documentation change
Repository and branch picker, GitHub connection settings and the Settings page, which includes the requirements reviewer's model

Settings page: an OpenAI endpoint section (base URL, API key, optional display name, whether a key is set, and a Remove action showing a 409 detail) shown only to the administrator; model pickers offer the openai adapter only when GET /settings offers it and label it with the endpoint's display name, or 'OpenAI' when the display name is empty
Shows delivery progress, agent questions, review findings and pull request links, and sends the user's answers and decisions

components.name: HTTP API
responsibilities: FastAPI application (app.api.main) exposing the auth, chat, requirements, architecture, API design, onboarding, workflows, settings and GitHub connector routes

Requires a valid access token of an active session on every router except sign-in, registration, its status, sign-out, POST /auth/refresh and the GitHub webhook endpoint; POST /auth/refresh authenticates by the refresh token alone, from the path-scoped refresh_token cookie or the JSON body

Auth routes set and clear both the access_token cookie and the refresh_token cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path /api/auth/refresh) and also return the refresh token in the JSON body for API clients
Validates input, bounds request sizes and maps Temporal and storage failures to 503 and session errors to 404/409/422
Starts, queries, signals and updates Temporal workflows for each session through the session services

Creates the database schemas at startup (including the auth sessions table, the model settings table, the OpenAI endpoint storage and the requirements store's baseline and task flow tables), runs the one-time model settings migration of old openai defaults to pi, and runs background loops: expired-document cleanup, expired and revoked auth session cleanup, Pi OAuth credential refresh, recovery of interrupted webhook mentions, deletion of superseded OpenAI endpoint versions no open execution pins (looked up by the OpenAIEndpointVersion search attribute) and deletion of the requirement layers of task flows closed longer than the retention period
At startup, cancels every still-running old-shape OnboardingWorkflow (top-level, without a parent task flow) started before this change; the step is idempotent, so later startups find none

Settings routes: return the OpenAI endpoint section shaped by role (base URL, display name and whether a key is set for the administrator; only the display name for anyone else), answer 403 to a non-administrator whose PUT contains the openai_endpoint section, and map a failed endpoint check or a changed base URL without a new key to 422, a blocked removal to 409, a removal with no endpoint saved to success and a missing SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY to 503

components.name: Auth module
responsibilities: Registers the first account as administrator and lets the administrator create and list accounts (app.auth)
Hashes passwords with salted scrypt and verifies them at sign-in

Starts a server-side session at sign-in and first-account registration, with its start time and last activity time, and issues a short-lived HS256 JWT access token signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET carrying the session id claim, sent as a bearer token or the HttpOnly access_token cookie, together with a long-lived opaque refresh token

Keeps sessions and their refresh tokens in PostgreSQL (app.auth.sessions), storing only a SHA-256 hash of each refresh token, never the token itself; a user's sessions are deleted with the user's account (foreign key cascade), so its tokens stop working at once

On every authenticated request, checks the access token's signature, expiry and session id claim and that its session still exists and is not revoked, rejecting tokens without a session id claim (issued before this change), and updates the session's last activity time, writing it at most once a minute per session (the write is skipped while the stored time is fresher)

Exchanges a refresh token at POST /auth/refresh for a new access token and a rotated refresh token, refusing a session past its idle limit or its absolute limit or one that is revoked; accepts the just-replaced refresh token for a grace period fixed at 30 seconds in code and revokes the whole session when an already-used refresh token is presented after it
Revokes the session named by the access token's session id claim, or by a refresh token in the request body, at sign-out

Rate-limits sign-in and registration attempts (AUTH_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE), and separately every refresh attempt (AUTH_REFRESH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE), per client address with the in-process sliding-window attempt limiter

Reads AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES (default 15, replacing AUTH_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS, which is no longer read), AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_DAYS (default 7), AUTH_SESSION_MAX_DAYS (default 30) and AUTH_REFRESH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE (default 30) from the backend configuration (app.config), documented in README.md and backend/.env.example
Deletes a session one day after it was revoked or passed its idle or absolute limit, run from the API's background cleanup

components.name: Session services
responsibilities: Per-flow services (app.requirements, app.architecture, app.api_design, app.onboarding, app.conversations, app.delivery service modules) that turn API calls into Temporal workflow starts, queries, signals and updates

Start a TaskWorkflow, with origin requirements or onboarding, for every new requirements interview (from the repository, branch and what needs to be done only, with no kind or intake answers) and onboarding, for every fork of a requirements, architecture, API design or onboarding interview session (linked to the original task's earlier stages, carrying over the forked interview's review state and, for a requirements session, the kind recorded at the fork point) and for every fix round on a closed delivery of a task or onboarding
The requirements intake (GET /requirements/intake) is removed

Pass finalize, with or without the force flag, to the requirements or onboarding interview; force is accepted at any point of the review (before it has run, during a running round, or after contradictions or a reviewer error) and writes the document at once; finalizing a requirements session with no kind recorded is refused with a conflict saying the kind is missing
Pass the retry of a failed review round from the requirements or onboarding session to its requirements review; retrying when the last round did not fail answers 409

Read session state, conversation, the recorded kind of task (or none), drafts, the requirements review's status, round, contradictions and any reviewer error, delivery progress and the task flow's ID and next stage's ID (architecture session, API design session, or the delivery of a bugfix or documentation change) from workflow queries for the API responses

Build the requirements lookup field of requirements, architecture, API design and onboarding session responses from the Requirements store records of the session's task flow (instead of session state or the checkout's contract files), each entry with its component or null
Hand authorised pull request mentions to the delivery workflow they belong to, for tasks and onboardings alike

List workflow executions with their repository, branch, task name, task origin, pending/skipped state, linked-task, waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings search attributes and the workflow registry (app.temporal.executions, app.temporal.registry). top_level lists task flows, chats, the old-shape requirements flows and the cancelled old-shape onboarding flows started before this change. parent lists a flow's direct children plus stages linked to it, and an old-shape flow's children as before. The origin filter lists only task flows of that origin. No onboarding ID is returned or accepted as a filter any more

For closed deliveries and task flows, clear the listed unresolved findings marker when a findings acceptance record (app.delivery.acceptances) exists for the closed delivery run, since a closed workflow can no longer update its own search attributes
The workflow_type filter for task flows lists only TaskWorkflow executions, so old-shape RequirementsWorkflow and OnboardingWorkflow executions appear only in the unfiltered (All) listing
Onboarding sessions of old-shape onboardings cancelled on deploy remain readable but accept no further actions (409)

components.name: Orchestration worker
responsibilities: Temporal worker on the main task queue (app.temporal.worker)
Runs LLMRequestWorkflow, TaskWorkflow, RequirementsWorkflow, RequirementsReviewWorkflow, ArchitectureWorkflow, ApiDesignWorkflow, OnboardingWorkflow and DeliveryWorkflow

TaskWorkflow (top-level per task, with an origin of requirements or onboarding): a task flow started by a requirements interview, or by the fork of a requirements session, creates only its requirements child at start. When the requirements interview is finalized, it creates the remaining children for the kind recorded at that moment: requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery for a new service or API change; requirements review and delivery for a bugfix; delivery for documentation. A task flow started by a fork of an architecture or API design session still creates the forked stage and pending children for the later stages at once, and an onboarding task flow still creates its onboarding interview, requirements review and delivery children up front. It holds each child pending until the stages it depends on have finished, then starts it, and closes skipped stages. It stays running (its Temporal status) for as long as any child is pending or running

RequirementsWorkflow starts without a kind of task: the interviewer proposes one from what needs to be done and records it with set_task_kind only after the user confirms it or names another, may change it any number of times until finalize and follows that kind's guidance from then on; the per-kind starting questions of the intake are gone. The session's opening is built from the task alone. Finalizing with no kind recorded is refused, which the API answers with 409

When a new requirements flow starts, an activity syncs the branch's contracts/requirements.json into the Requirements store's baseline for that repository and branch (the repository overwriting stored differences, components inferred by an LLM from contracts/architecture.json for requirements without one) and links the task flow to it; a fork's task flow is linked to the same baseline and gets a copy of the requirements created in the source session

Interviewer, architecture and onboarding activities write each requirement change to the task flow's layer of the Requirements store as soon as their tools make it, so the store is current while the turn runs; the architecture agent assigns requirements without a component once it defines components

Delivery writes requirements to contracts/requirements.json as today, each with its component field, and commits contracts/architecture.md and contracts/architecture.json; an API change replaces both, a skipped stage keeps both

While resolving merge conflicts, delivery maps changed or renumbered requirements to their counterparts (same ID with similar content, or same title and description under another ID), updates the Requirements store with the mapping and asks the user about the rest through the delivery's agent questions

TaskWorkflow starts the requirements review, created at finalize, when the requirements interview is finalized as a new service, API change or bugfix (onboarding: when the onboarding interview is finalized, except an architecture-only onboarding, whose review closes as skipped). It starts the next stage only once the review passes or the user continues despite contradictions: the delivery of a bugfix or onboarding, or the architecture of a new service or API change. It starts the API design when the architecture is finalized or skipped, and for documentation it starts the delivery as soon as the requirements are finalized

A requirements session written because it was idle for a day writes its document without a review, whatever kind is recorded (or none), and the task flow creates no further children; with no delivery child it then closes as cancelled. An onboarding interview idle for a day still closes its precreated review and delivery children as skipped, so its task flow closes as cancelled

RequirementsReviewWorkflow (one child per task across all its rounds): in each round an LLM checks the session's requirements against each other and against the existing service's requirements the task has not retired; for an onboarding that replaces an existing contract, the drafted requirements are also checked against that contract's requirements. From the second round on, the reviewer is given both the diff of the requirement records since its previous round (added, changed and removed, with their texts) and the contradiction questions with the user's answers. It returns the contradictions to the requirements or onboarding interview, which asks the user one question per contradiction. Once all are answered, the interview hands the updated requirements back for the next round. Rounds are unlimited. It closes as passed when no contradictions remain, or as continued anyway with the remaining contradictions when the user finalizes with force

When a review round's LLM activity still fails after its Temporal retries (provider unavailable or invalid output), the round is marked failed with the reviewer's error and treated like a round with contradictions found (none listed): the session shows the error and the user can either retry the round through a retry action, like retrying a failed turn, which runs the same round again with the same input, or continue with force; nothing later starts on its own

Finalize with force writes the requirements document at once whatever the review's state: a running review round is cancelled, and a review that has not run yet is closed as continued anyway with no contradictions; the remaining contradictions of the last finished round are listed in the document
Requirements and onboarding reviews use the same requirements_review model settings entry

Requirements and onboarding interviews keep the review's status, round and contradictions for their session responses, write the requirements document only after the review passes or is forced, and list the remaining contradictions in it when it was forced. A forked requirements or onboarding interview copies the review state (status, round and contradictions) of the session it was forked from at the fork point, and its new task flow's review continues from that round

OnboardingWorkflow is the onboarding interview stage of an onboarding TaskWorkflow: it no longer starts its own delivery but hands its finalized contract, including contracts/architecture.md and contracts/architecture.json, to the task flow, whose delivery child verifies, reviews and pushes it (code generation runs under that delivery). Fix rounds on a closed onboarding's pull request and forks of an onboarding interview start a new onboarding TaskWorkflow, as they do for tasks. Onboarding never uses set_task_kind and is unchanged by the kind moving into the interview

TaskWorkflow keeps the task's short name: written by an LLM from what needs to be done at start and rewritten from the finalized requirements; a task flow started by a fork or a fix round on a closed delivery copies the original task's name with a '(fork)' or '(fix)' suffix, and a fork's name is still rewritten when its requirements are finalized

TaskWorkflow closes with its delivery child's status once every child, including the earlier stages it links to from a fork or fix round, has closed; it closes as cancelled when the delivery was skipped or when no delivery child was ever created (idle-written requirements session)

Stage workflows keep their own waiting-for-user state (unanswered interviewer or contradiction questions, a failed review round, coding agent questions, open review findings, a skip proposal or a contract decision) and unresolved-findings state as search attributes, cleared when the flow closes so a closed flow is never waiting (FR-110)

Stages report every change of their waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings state to their TaskWorkflow, which aggregates its children's states into its own WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings search attributes

Stage workflows report their hand-off (requirements interview finalized with its recorded kind or idle-written, onboarding interview finalized or idle-written, review passed or forced, architecture finalized or skip confirmed, API design finalized, pull request merged or closed) to their TaskWorkflow instead of starting the next stage themselves, and on closing signal every task flow they are linked into
Activities for LLM interviewer turns and drafting, requirements review rounds, writing the requirements, architecture and OpenAPI documents, and naming task flows
Activities for repository checkout and contract reading, pushing deliveries, documentation and onboardings, and opening or updating pull requests with LLM-written text
Classifies mentions of the GitHub App, replies to them and answers clarifications
DeliveryWorkflow runs code generation, implementation, test generation, verification with diagnosis and repair rounds, code review rounds and the push as child workflows on the other task queues

Requirements executions started before this change keep running in their old shape (stages under a RequirementsWorkflow) and are not migrated; old-shape top-level OnboardingWorkflows are cancelled on deploy, together with their delivery and code generation children, and have to be started again

components.name: Codegen worker
responsibilities: Temporal worker on the codegen task queue running CodegenWorkflow (app.codegen.worker)
Runs openapi-generator to turn the finalized OpenAPI document into server code for the chosen language
Writes the generated code to GENERATED_CODE_DIR for the next stages

components.name: Sandbox worker
responsibilities: One host process with a Temporal worker per sandboxed stage and its own task queue: implementation, test generation, verification, diagnosis, code review and documentation, one activity at a time each (app.agent_workflows.worker)
Builds agent images and starts, monitors and removes coding agent containers through a Docker daemon (app.docker_agents)

Passes the workspace, LLM settings and provider credentials into containers and re-logs their output; for the openai adapter the base URL and API key come from the OpenAI endpoint version pinned by the stage's flow, read at each agent run, and the key is redacted from the re-logged output
Writes a snapshot of the stage's task flow's requirements, read from the Requirements store at each agent run, into the workspace for the agents' read-requirements tool
Keeps the workspace of an agent that paused with questions and resumes it with the user's answers
Builds the service from its root Dockerfile and runs the contract test suites against it (Python and Java test-suite images) for verification and baseline checks

components.name: Coding agent containers
responsibilities: Isolated Docker containers, one per agent run, built from app/agent_workflows/Dockerfile with the role's agent.py
Implementation, test generation, diagnosis, code review and documentation agents that read and write only their mounted workspace
Call the LLM through the LangChain, Pi or Claude adapter with the stage's model settings
Read requirements through the read-requirements tool over the task flow's requirements snapshot copied into the workspace, as they have no database access
Pause with questions for the user by saving their state in the workspace
Have no access to Temporal, PostgreSQL or the Docker daemon

components.name: LLM adapters
responsibilities: Build the chat model for a workflow from its model settings (app.llm.factory): OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini through LangChain, the Pi coding agent CLI, or Claude through the Claude Agent SDK

Take the OpenAI-compatible base URL and API key from the stored OpenAI endpoint passed in with the model settings (in the workers) or from the container's environment set by the sandbox worker (in agent containers), never from the process's own OPENAI_* configuration
Run the LangGraph tool-calling agent with the session tools (requirements, architecture, API design, repository, documents and questions tools in app.tools)

Offer the read-requirements tool to every agent of every stage, filtering by component, requirement ID or free text and bound to the agent's task flow: in the workers it reads the Requirements store, in agent containers the flow's requirements snapshot in the workspace

The requirements interviewer's tools set each requirement's component when recording or updating it (null while the flow has no architecture components), and the architecture agent's tools assign every requirement without a component to one of the components it defines
Normalize the questions the LLM asks the user
Optionally trace LLM calls to Langfuse

components.name: GitHub connector
responsibilities: Stores the shared GitHub App connection with its private key and webhook secret encrypted with Fernet (app.github.storage)
Calls the GitHub REST API as the app: installation tokens, repositories, branches, manifest conversion, webhook configuration, pull requests and comments (app.github.client)
Checks out and pushes branches with git using installation tokens (app.github.checkout)
Verifies webhook signatures, deduplicates deliveries and comments, and admits only authorised mentions on the app's pull requests (app.github.webhooks)

components.name: Document storage
responsibilities: Stores uploaded attachments and generated documents with their metadata in PostgreSQL and their originals on disk under DOCUMENT_STORAGE_DIR (app.documents)
Parses uploads into searchable session passages
Deletes expired documents

components.name: Model settings
responsibilities: Internal storage of the adapter, model and thinking level chosen for each LLM workflow type (app.settings), now including a requirements_review entry for the requirements reviewer of tasks and onboardings alike, separate from the code review entry
Knows the models and thinking levels each provider offers
Provides the settings the workers and agent containers use for their LLM calls

Stores the single shared OpenAI endpoint as versions: each save that changes the base URL or API key adds a new version (base URL and the API key encrypted with Fernet under the new SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and makes it current; the display name is kept apart from the versions, is optional, and a display-name-only change saves without a new version or check. Provides a version, decrypted, to the API's model listing, the workers and the sandbox worker in place of the OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY environment variables, which are no longer read; without a valid SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY an endpoint with a key cannot be saved or read and the request answers 503

Running work keeps the endpoint it started with: every top-level flow (task flow or chat) pins the current endpoint version ID when it starts (no key in Temporal history) and passes it to its children, whose activities and agent runs read that version until the flow ends; a task flow started by a fork or a fix round pins the version that is current when it starts, not the original flow's; flows without a pinned version (started before this change, or started while none was saved) read the current one. Superseded versions are kept, however long that takes, until no open execution pins them, and then deleted

Checks the endpoint with GET {base URL}/models only when the base URL or API key changes, with the new key or, for an empty key field, the stored one; the stored key is reused only while the base URL stays the same, so a changed base URL with an empty key field is refused with 422 unless the key is explicitly set to empty; the endpoint and the workflow settings of the same request are saved in one transaction, so a failed check saves nothing

Removes the endpoint (every version and the display name) unless a workflow type's saved adapter is openai, and reports those workflow types when it refuses; removing when no endpoint is saved is a successful no-op

Offers the openai adapter only while an endpoint base URL is saved, and uses pi as the default adapter of a workflow type with no saved adapter while none is saved, also when filling in missing workflow types at startup; a saved openai choice stays and its runs fail with a clear error until the endpoint is set up

One-time, idempotent startup migration: while no endpoint is saved, every workflow type row that still holds the old default (adapter openai with the old default model) is switched to the pi default; rows the user changed are left as they are

components.name: PostgreSQL
responsibilities: Stores application data in the app schema: users, GitHub connection, pull requests, webhook deliveries and comments, mention admissions, delivery mentions, onboarding sessions, documents and passages, workflow settings, the workflow registry and the task flows' requirements
Stores Temporal's persistence and visibility databases in deployment

components.name: Temporal server
responsibilities: Persists workflow state and dispatches workflow and activity tasks to the workers by task queue
Keeps the Repository and Branch search attributes used to list executions; OnboardingId is no longer set on new executions or returned

Keeps the FlowState (pending or skipped, overriding the Temporal status in listings), TaskName and LinkedTaskFlows (keyword list of task flows a stage is linked into by a fork or fix round) search attributes, upserted by the workflows
Keeps the new TaskOrigin keyword search attribute (requirements or onboarding), set when a TaskWorkflow starts, which the origin filter queries
Keeps the WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings boolean search attributes, upserted by stages and task flows, so listings carry the backend-computed highlight and marker
Keeps the new OpenAIEndpointVersion keyword search attribute, the OpenAI endpoint version a flow pinned at its start, so superseded versions still pinned by open executions are not deleted

components.name: GitHub
responsibilities: External service: the GitHub REST API at api.github.com and git hosting of the repositories the shared GitHub App installation can access
Issues installation tokens, converts app manifests and holds the app's webhook configuration, pull requests and comments
Delivers signed webhook events for pull request conversation and inline review comments

components.name: LLM provider
responsibilities: External service: the model endpoints chosen in the model settings (OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Google Gemini, the providers behind the Pi CLI, or Anthropic's Claude)
Answers the chat, interviewer, drafting, requirements review, code review, pull request text, mention classification and coding agent model calls

components.name: Langfuse
responsibilities: External, optional tracing service that receives traces of LLM calls, of the main and codegen queues' activity executions and of sandboxed stage operations
Used only when LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL are set and LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED is not false

components.name: Requirements store
responsibilities: New module (app.requirements.store) keeping a project's requirements in PostgreSQL in two layers: a shared baseline per repository and branch holding the requirements of the branch's contract, and per task flow the flow's own changes stored on top of that baseline

Holds each requirement with its ID, category, title, description, priority, component (an architecture component name or null) and, in a flow's layer, whether it was created, changed, removed or retired by the flow

Syncs the branch's contracts/requirements.json into the branch's baseline when a new requirements flow starts, the repository's version overwriting the stored baseline where they differ; the starting flow is linked to that baseline
The baseline is not versioned: flows already running on the branch see an updated baseline at once under their own changes

Infers, during the sync, the component of a baseline requirement that has none by an LLM call using the requirements interviewer's model settings entry, matching it to the component responsibilities in contracts/architecture.json, and leaves it null when no architecture.json exists or no component fits

Applies every change of a flow's requirements (recorded, updated, removed, renumbered, retired or kept, and component assignments) to that flow's layer as soon as it happens, never to the baseline or another flow's layer
Copies the requirements created in a forked session's flow layer into the fork's new task flow, linked to the same branch baseline

Answers reads of a task flow's effective requirements (its baseline overlaid by its own layer) filtered by component, requirement ID or free-text search, never including another task flow's layer, for the read-requirements tool and the requirement lookups of session responses

Deletes a task flow's layer once the flow has been completed or cancelled for longer than REQUIREMENTS_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30, read from the backend configuration in app.config and documented in README.md and backend/.env.example), run from the API's background cleanup; branch baselines are kept, as the next sync refreshes them

data_flows.description: JSON (and multipart for chat attachments) over HTTP under /api through the frontend's proxy, with the access_token cookie on every request and the refresh_token cookie only on POST /api/auth/refresh; the client polls sessions and workflow lists for progress.

In-process calls: credentials for registration and sign-in, refresh tokens to exchange, session ids or refresh tokens to revoke at sign-out, and the access token (bearer or cookie) of every protected request to resolve the signed-in user and its active session.

Users with their scrypt password hashes and creation times, and auth sessions with their user, start time, last activity time, revocation and the hashes of the current and just-replaced refresh tokens with the replacement time, read and written with psycopg; a session check on every authenticated request and a last-activity write at most once a minute per session.
In-process calls with validated session actions: messages, answers, forks, finalize, skip, checkout, contract decisions, agent answers, findings decisions, stage retries and workflow list filters.

Temporal client gRPC calls: start TaskWorkflows (with TaskOrigin and the pinned OpenAIEndpointVersion) and chats with search attributes, send signals and updates to the task flow and its stages (including finalize with force and the retry of a failed review round), run queries for session and review state, and list executions by visibility queries over ParentWorkflowId, LinkedTaskFlows, FlowState, TaskOrigin, OpenAIEndpointVersion and the other search attributes.
Workflow registry entries, onboarding sessions and delivery mentions, read and written with psycopg.
In-process calls: connect, check and remove the app, list repositories and branches, and hand over raw webhook deliveries with their signature for verification and mention admission.
The connection with its Fernet-encrypted private key and webhook secret, the app's pull requests, handled webhook deliveries and comments, and mention admissions.
In-process calls: chat attachments to store, and document IDs to stream back as downloads.
Document metadata and parsed session passages; the originals are written to files on disk.

The workflow_settings rows with the model settings of every LLM workflow type, the OpenAI endpoint versions (base URL and Fernet-encrypted API key) with the current one marked, and the display name, read and written with psycopg in one transaction per save.

Workflow and activity tasks of the main task queue over gRPC. The worker returns results, starts TaskWorkflow stage children (pending ones wait for a start signal from their task flow) and starts child workflows on the codegen and sandboxed stage queues. Stage workflows signal their task flow at each hand-off and on every change of their waiting-for-user and unresolved-findings state, and, when they close, every task flow in their LinkedTaskFlows. In each review round the requirements or onboarding interview signals the review with the current requirements, the diff since the previous round and the contradiction questions with the user's answers, and the review signals back the contradictions found. The task flow signals pending stages to start or close as skipped, and workflows upsert their search attributes.
CodegenWorkflow tasks with the OpenAPI document and language over gRPC; the result names the generated code directory.

Implementation, test generation, verification, diagnosis, review and documentation workflow tasks over gRPC, each on its own task queue; results carry workspaces, verdicts, findings or agent questions.

In-process calls with the conversation, session tools and the workflow's model settings for interviewer turns, drafting, chat answers, task flow names, pull request text, mention classification and replies, and the component inference of synced requirements against architecture.json's component responsibilities.
In-process calls to check out the session's branch and read its contract, push deliveries and onboardings to new branches, open or update pull requests and post mention replies.
Parses uploads into passages and writes generated requirements, architecture and OpenAPI documents.

Reads the model settings of the workflow type an LLM activity runs for and, for the openai adapter, the OpenAI endpoint version the flow pinned at its start (or the current one when none is pinned) with its decrypted key, at each activity run; reads the current version ID when a top-level flow starts.

Docker CLI calls to a dedicated Docker daemon: builds the agent image, copies in the workspace (contract, generated code, tests, review findings, answers, and the task flow's requirements snapshot) and the stage's model settings file, passes provider credentials as environment variables (for openai, the stored endpoint's base URL, rewritten for the container network, and its key), and copies the workspace and agent state back out.

Reads each stage's model settings to pass into its agent container and, for the openai adapter, the OpenAI endpoint version pinned by the stage's flow (or the current one when none is pinned) with its decrypted key, at each agent run.
In-process calls inside the container: the agent runs the adapter code copied into its image with the stage's model settings file.
Admitted pull request mentions handed to the delivery workflow they belong to (of a task or an onboarding) as Temporal signals or updates, delivered through the Temporal server.
Generated server code passed as files under GENERATED_CODE_DIR on the shared /data volume, which the implementation stage copies into its workspace.

REST calls over HTTPS through httpx, authenticated with RS256 app JWTs and installation tokens (installations, repositories, branches, manifest conversion, webhook configuration, pull requests and comments), and git clone and push over HTTPS with installation tokens.
Webhook deliveries (issue_comment and pull_request_review_comment events) POSTed to /connectors/github/events with the X-Hub-Signature-256, X-GitHub-Event and X-GitHub-Delivery headers.

Model calls over HTTPS with the conversation, tools and the workflow's model and thinking level, through LangChain clients, the Pi CLI or the Claude Agent SDK, from the workers and from inside agent containers with the forwarded credentials.
Traces of LLM calls (LangChain callback handler, Claude plugin hook) exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys, with secrets redacted and content capture optional.
Spans of sandboxed stage operations (agent runs, diagnosis, review) over HTTPS; the trace context and Langfuse settings are passed into agent containers as environment variables.

Spans of the main queue's activity executions (interviewer turns, drafting, document writing, mention handling), tagged with the Temporal workflow, run, activity ID and attempt by the trace_activity decorator (app.temporal.tracing), exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys when tracing is enabled; replayed workflow code is never traced.

Spans of the generate-server-code activity (CodegenWorkflow), tagged with the Temporal workflow, run, activity ID and attempt by the trace_activity decorator (app.temporal.tracing), exported over HTTPS with the Langfuse keys when tracing is enabled.

In-process calls: read the workflow settings, offered adapters and models and the OpenAI endpoint for GET /settings, and save workflow settings together with an endpoint change or removal for PUT /settings, with the signed-in user's administrator flag already checked.
GET {base URL}/models over HTTPS through httpx with the API key as a bearer token, to check an OpenAI endpoint before it is saved and to list the endpoint's models for the model pickers.

In-process calls from activities: the branch contract's requirements and architecture components to sync at requirements flow start, each requirement change (record, update, remove, renumber, retire, keep, component assignment) as it happens, the fork copy of a source session's created requirements and the merge-conflict mapping of changed or renumbered requirements.
Baseline requirement rows per repository and branch and overlay rows per task flow, read and written with psycopg; each sync, fork copy or change in one transaction.
In-process reads of a session's task flow's requirements (session's own, existing service's and retired, with components) for the requirements lookup field of session responses.
In-process read-requirements tool calls from agents running in the workers, filtered by component, requirement ID or free text and bound to the agent's task flow ID.
In-process read of the stage's task flow's requirements at each agent run, written into the workspace as the snapshot the containers' read-requirements tool serves.
In-process calls from the background cleanup loop: the IDs of task flows closed longer than the retention period, whose requirement layers are deleted; and schema creation at startup.

technology_choices.choice: Python 3.12 with FastAPI, served by uvicorn
technology_choices.rationale: Required by TR-1; async request handling fits the Temporal and httpx clients.

technology_choices.choice: Temporal (temporalio Python SDK, server 1.32) with separate task queues for the main, codegen and each sandboxed stage worker
technology_choices.rationale: Long-running sessions that wait on the user, retries of single stages and child workflows per stage; separate queues keep each stage to one container at a time.

technology_choices.choice: PostgreSQL 16 through psycopg 3 for application data and Temporal persistence; uploaded originals and generated code on a disk volume
technology_choices.rationale: Required by TR-1; one database server serves both the app and Temporal.

technology_choices.choice: React 19 with TypeScript, built with Vite, react-markdown for rendered documents
technology_choices.rationale: Required by TR-1.

technology_choices.choice: LangChain/LangGraph tool-calling agents over OpenAI-compatible endpoints or Google Gemini, plus the Pi coding agent CLI and the Claude Agent SDK as alternative adapters, chosen per workflow type in the model settings
technology_choices.rationale: Lets each workflow use a different provider and model without code changes.

technology_choices.choice: Docker containers started through a separate Docker-in-Docker daemon (docker:dind under the Sysbox runtime) whose socket only the sandbox worker mounts, on its own network without private addresses
technology_choices.rationale: TR-2: agents must not reach Temporal, the database or Docker.

technology_choices.choice: openapi-generator, run as a subprocess by the codegen worker
technology_choices.rationale: Produces server scaffolding from the finalized OpenAPI document before the coding agents fill it in.

technology_choices.choice: One shared GitHub App: REST API through httpx with RS256 app JWTs and installation tokens, git CLI for checkout and push, signed webhooks (HMAC-SHA256) for pull request comment mentions
technology_choices.rationale: Lets the instance act on repositories without user tokens and receive mentions.

technology_choices.choice: Short-lived HS256 access JWTs via PyJWT with a session id claim, opaque random refresh tokens (secrets module) stored only as SHA-256 hashes, scrypt password hashes from hashlib, Fernet (cryptography) encryption of the GitHub App key and webhook secret with GITHUB_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and of the OpenAI API key with a dedicated SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
technology_choices.rationale: NFR-2, NFR-8, NFR-10 to NFR-14 and TR-13 to TR-15: the access token stays a stateless JWT for its signature and expiry, while the session id lets every request check revocation; a refresh token only has to be looked up, so an opaque value whose hash is stored keeps a database leak from yielding usable tokens.

technology_choices.choice: Optional Langfuse tracing of LLM calls and stage operations, also from inside agent containers
technology_choices.rationale: Active only when the Langfuse keys and base URL are set (LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED defaults to true but can turn it off); secrets are redacted from traces.

technology_choices.choice: Docker Compose (Coolify): frontend with nginx, api, worker, codegen-worker, sandbox-worker, sandbox daemon, PostgreSQL, Temporal and Temporal UI; the root Dockerfile builds the API alone with its own PostgreSQL on port 8080 as a non-root user
technology_choices.rationale: TR-3: the root image is a self-contained service for contract tests; deployments use backend/Dockerfile.

technology_choices.choice: A TaskWorkflow per task or onboarding on the main queue starts its stages as Temporal children and carries a TaskOrigin search attribute. A requirements task flow (new or forked from a requirements session) starts with only its requirements child and creates the later children, pending, when the requirements are finalized, for the kind the RequirementsResult carries; architecture and API design forks and onboardings still create their children up front. A stage not yet allowed to work waits for a start signal and carries FlowState=pending, and a stage that will never run closes with FlowState=skipped. Links of forked or fix-round task flows to earlier stages are the LinkedTaskFlows keyword-list search attribute on those stages. The OnboardingId attribute is dropped.
technology_choices.rationale: FR-125 to FR-140, FR-159, FR-164, FR-166, FR-229 and FR-235: the kind is only known for certain at finalize, so creating children then avoids creating and skipping children of a kind the task turned out not to be; Temporal has no not-yet-started executions or second parents, so pending, skipped, linked and origin are expressed with search attributes GET /workflows can filter on, keeping NFR-7's existing fields and Temporal statuses underneath.

technology_choices.choice: Computed in the backend: each stage and onboarding upserts WaitingForUser and UnresolvedFindings search attributes as its state changes and clears WaitingForUser when it closes; the TaskWorkflow aggregates its children's states, signalled by them, into its own attributes; for closed flows the listing clears UnresolvedFindings when the existing findings acceptance record exists for the delivery run; GET /workflows returns both as new fields. Executions started before this change carry neither attribute and are listed without highlight or marker (the fields are null for them)
technology_choices.rationale: User's choice to compute the highlight in the backend; search attributes let the listing show it without querying every child, the acceptance record already holds acceptances given after a flow closed (FR-142, FR-143), closed flows are never waiting (FR-110), and the listing only gains fields (NFR-7). User chose not to backfill old-shape flows: they are only listed.

technology_choices.choice: A RequirementsReviewWorkflow per task or onboarding on the main queue, created pending by the TaskWorkflow and started on finalize. It runs every round of the review in one execution, calling the LLM through the existing adapters with the requirements_review model settings entry (shared by tasks and onboardings). From the second round on it is given the requirements diff plus the contradiction questions and answers. It talks to the interview stage by Temporal signals and closes as passed, continued anyway or skipped. A round whose LLM activity fails after Temporal's retries is marked failed with the error; the user retries it through a retry action like a failed turn, or forces past it; force cancels a running round.
technology_choices.rationale: FR-144 to FR-158 and FR-153: a child flow of its own shown on the Flows page, with unlimited rounds that wait on the user's answers. The diff tells the reviewer what changed and the answers tell it how the user meant to resolve each contradiction (FR-147). One settings entry keeps Settings simple (FR-148). The user chose that a failed review round can be retried like a failed turn or forced past, and that force writes the document at once even while a round runs.

technology_choices.choice: Cancelled on deploy: an idempotent startup step of the API cancels every running top-level OnboardingWorkflow (no parent task flow) with its children; they stay listed as cancelled in the All view and must be started again.
technology_choices.rationale: User's choice; avoids keeping the onboarding ID field and the old onboarding flow shape alive alongside the task flow shape (FR-159, FR-164).

technology_choices.choice: One shared OpenAI endpoint stored as versions by the Model settings component in PostgreSQL; each top-level flow (task flow, chat) pins the current version ID at start, passes it to its children and carries it as the new OpenAIEndpointVersion keyword search attribute, and every activity and agent run reads the pinned version; an API background loop deletes superseded versions no open execution pins; OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY are removed from the configuration and not imported; the default adapter becomes pi while no endpoint is saved, and a one-time startup migration switches rows still holding the old openai default to pi; the stored key is only reused for an unchanged base URL
technology_choices.rationale: FR-174 to FR-182 and TR-7. The user chose that running work keeps the endpoint it started with: pinning a version ID keeps the key out of Temporal history while a value set on the Settings page still reaches new flows in every process without a restart. The startup fill-in saved openai for every workflow type, so without the migration removal (FR-182) would be blocked for good. Not sending the stored key to a new address keeps the secret from leaking to another host (user's choice). Removal deletes every version, as no workflow type can use openai by then.

technology_choices.topic: Migration of in-flight requirements task flows
technology_choices.choice: No migration and no Temporal workflow versioning: requirements task flows already running at deploy (started with a kind, with all children created up front) are left as they are and replay against the new TaskWorkflow and RequirementsWorkflow code; any that fail on replay (non-determinism) are accepted as lost and have to be started again.
technology_choices.rationale: User's choice; the change is breaking anyway and keeping the old code paths behind workflow.patched is not worth it.

technology_choices.choice: An auth sessions table in the app schema of PostgreSQL, one row per sign-in with a cascading foreign key to its user, holding the start and last activity times, revocation and the current and just-replaced refresh token hashes with the replacement time; rotation replaces the hash in one transaction with a row lock, the replaced token stays valid for a fixed 30-second grace period, and reuse of an older token revokes the row; last activity is written at most once a minute per session; the API's background cleanup deletes a session one day after it was revoked or passed its idle or absolute limit
technology_choices.rationale: NFR-10 to NFR-12 and FR-239 to FR-241: PostgreSQL is already the app's store and is reached on each request anyway; keeping the previous hash allows the grace period without a token history table; the row lock keeps concurrent refreshes from both rotating. The user chose a fixed grace period, a throttled last-activity write (one read per request; a minute is negligible against a 7-day idle limit), keeping dead sessions one day before deletion, and deleting a user's sessions with the account.

technology_choices.choice: Browser Web Locks API (navigator.locks) around each refresh, with a BroadcastChannel announcing its result to the other tabs
technology_choices.rationale: FR-245: a named lock serialises refreshes across tabs of the same origin without a server change, and the broadcast lets waiting tabs reuse the new expiry instead of refreshing again.

technology_choices.choice: Tables in the app schema of PostgreSQL, created by the API at startup with the other schemas: an unversioned baseline per repository and branch synced from contracts/requirements.json, and per task flow an overlay of the flow's own changes keyed by task flow ID and requirement ID, read as the live baseline overlaid by the flow's layer; written through psycopg by worker activities (never from workflow code); components of legacy requirements inferred by an LLM call in the sync activity with the requirements interviewer's model settings; coding agents read a per-run JSON snapshot of the flow's effective requirements in their workspace instead of the database; free-text search uses PostgreSQL text matching over ID, title and description; layers of closed flows deleted by the API's background cleanup after REQUIREMENTS_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30)
technology_choices.rationale: FR-247 to FR-260: PostgreSQL is already the app's store; a shared live baseline avoids re-syncing and re-inferring the same branch per flow and keeps running flows on the branch's latest contract (user's choices) while overlays keep flows isolated (FR-258); activities keep Temporal workflows deterministic; the snapshot keeps TR-2's isolation of agent containers; reusing the interviewer's settings entry avoids a new Settings entry; a configurable 30-day retention bounds storage of closed flows (user's choices).
